name: aubio
why: Command-line onset, pitch, and beat extraction from audio is a genuine door into music information retrieval and makes audio into annotations.

brief.what_it_is: aubio is a C library, with a Python module and command-line tools, for extracting annotations from audio. It listens to an audio signal and marks events such as note onsets, pitch, beats and tempo, quiet and loud regions, and MFCC features. The tools take audio input (sound files, or live audio for real-time use) and print results such as timestamps, pitch values, or MIDI-like notes, while aubiocut slices a sound file at onset or beat points. The executables are aubio, aubiocut, aubioonset, aubiopitch, aubiomfcc, aubiotrack, aubionotes and aubioquiet. The algorithms are causal, so they can also run in real time with low delay.
brief.why_it_exists: The authors say these tasks are difficult, so they wanted them gathered in a dedicated library. The README frames aubio as a library to label music and sounds, detecting events such as a drum hit, the frequency of a note, or the tempo of a rhythmic melody.
brief.how_it_works: Algorithms are implemented in C and run causally, so they can process audio as it arrives. The Python interface is written in C so that aubio arrays appear directly as NumPy arrays. The README does not describe the detection methods in detail beyond naming them: several onset detection methods, several pitch detection methods, and tempo and beat tracking.

commands_seen.context: Build instruction from the README for compiling the C library. The README says aubio compiles on Linux, Mac OS X, Windows, Cygwin and iOS.
Build instruction from the README for compiling the Python module.

brief.install_notes: No Homebrew caveats were given. As of version 0.4.0 aubio has no required dependencies. Optional dependencies are libav, libsndfile, libsamplerate and FFTW, and none of these are needed on Apple platforms. On Linux, aubio can be built with JACK. On Apple machines, JackOSX and AudioToolbox can be used. The README points to the manual's installing page for fuller instructions. Badges show PyPI and conda-forge distributions exist, so the Python module can also be installed from those.
brief.standout: Causal algorithms that work in real time as well as offline, combined with a dependency-free C core. The name is a deliberate typo of audio, and the README warns that some errors are likely in the results.
brief.status: unknown. The GitHub README has CI badges, a Zenodo DOI and a commits-since-last-release badge, but it shows no release date or last commit. The homepage copyright reads 2003-2018, and its 'Latest news' and 'Latest changes' sections showed no dates in the fetched text.
brief.caveats: Licence is GPL: the homepage says aubio is not MIT or BSD and that commercial users should contact the author. The Python module needs a separate build step (./setup.py build). Optional features depend on which libraries are present at build time. The README warns that the name is a typo of audio and that errors are likely in the results. The homepage text is dated 2003-2018 and the status is unclear.
quotes: aubio is a library to label music and sounds. It listens to audio signals and attempts to detect events.
The name aubio comes from _audio_ with a typo: some errors are likely to be found in the results.
To increase the fun, we have made these algorithms work in a causal way, so as to be used in real time applications with as low delay as possible.
